name: Euthanasia
overview: Scripture affirms the sanctity of human life as made in the image of God, commanding that we must not kill (Genesis 9:6; Exodus 20:13). While Ecclesiastes acknowledges that there is a time and season for all things, including death (Ecclesiastes 3:1), it also warns against dying before one's appointed time (Ecclesiastes 7:17) and teaches that no one has power over the spirit to prolong or shorten life at will (Ecclesiastes 8:8). Believers are called to endure suffering with patience and hope, trusting in God's sovereign timing rather than hastening death (Romans 5:3). This biblical perspective challenges the practice of euthanasia, including passive euthanasia, as it contravenes God's authority over life and death.
